Vaal Dam sluice gates open: Floods

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Hundreds of residents around the Vaal dam have had to evacuate their homes when 12 sluice gates on the dam were opened. Could there have been earlier warning signs?

Unique Selling Point:
Rescue operations were ongoing throughout the weekend to evacuate homes on and around the Vaal dam and river as water levels continue to rise amidst high rain fall. Water affairs have opened 12 sluice gates to manage the inflow, but was it too later?

Summary:
Twelve of the 24 sluice gates on the Vaal Dam have been opened. Given the high rainfall and water moving in from Standerton where the bridge, connecting Mpumalanga and Gauteng have been closed all weekend, rising water levels will urge water affairs to open more sluice gates this week. Problem is, it is all happening at once and hundreds of people living lower downstream have been and will be evacuating their houses.

Further information:
Kyle Streicher and his family had two hours to evacuate their home near Barrage in Vanderbijlpark on Saturday. They returned on Sunday to see whether there was anything to salvage, but their entire home and belongings have been destroyed. Their house was built higher than the 100-year flood mark. And this is where the argument comes in:

Firstly: Affected families are angry with water affairs, saying they did not receive proper warning to evacuate in time.

Secondly: the gates were opened all at once and should have been done weeks prior to the high rainfall. They say the department of water and sanitation does not have skilled people in place to determine when the gates must be opened. Floods could have been avoided.



Two years ago, I did a story on the same topic. People on the Vaal and Lower Orange were concerned that given high rainfall at the time, the department did not open the sluice gates in time and a flood could have destroyed everything. Luckily for them, it turned out that it was never necessary to open many gates. But this year, is an entirely different story. What people have been complaining and warning about, now happened.



But the department of water and sanitation in Gauteng is actually a very highly skilled group of people. They say, they opened the first sluice gates on 7 February and there was sufficient warning. They add that people who live below the 100-year flood line mark had it coming as they were never supposed to build their houses there.

VAAL DAM FLOODING SCRIPT

VO
If you had less than two hours to evacuate your house, what would you take with you and what would you leave behind?

UPS DRAMA

VO
That was the horrifying reality facing hundreds of families this week, forced to flee devastating floods. People living around the Vaal dam in the Free state and Bloemhof dam in the North West had less than two hours to ensure the safety of their families and pets and move their belongings to higher ground.

VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
09:57:30:29
“Ek het nog hierso gestaan dan sien jy gaan jou een tenthuis, dan gaan jou ander tenthuis en dan hoor jy hoe vat hy jou houthuis, al daai goed so saam”.=
TRANSLATION: I was standing here, and I saw my tent house go and then I saw the other one go and then it took my wooden cabin, all my things…”

VO
Fanie Smith is devastated. Having worked on the gold mines all his life, in 2016 he used his pension and savings to buy his dream-house on the Vaal river between Parys and Potchefstroom.

VO
This wasn’t his first experience of flooding, and he took precautions when the water started rising.

SUPER@FANIE SMITH
VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
09:52:45:02
“Hy het opgetel dan vat hy nette en dakkie voor weg en met die jare kom hy so op. Hierdie jaar is die eerste jaar wat ek hom so hoog sien”
TRANSLATION: When the water came up, it took shading nets and roofs. This is the first year the levels are so high.

VO
He measured the levels hourly, and set an alarm to wake him during the night so he could monitor markers he had made. He never imagined the magnitude of the flood coming his way.

SUPER@FANIE SMITH
VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
09:55:59:15
“So elke 15/20 minute kan jy sien tel hy op tel hy op…”
TRANSLATION: “The water kept rising, every 15 to 20 minutes”

VO
In the end, all he could do was watch as the water swallowed all he’d built.


LINK
VAAL FLOODS CARD 1
P1021978
“We watched the visuals of water levels rising and people’s homes being completely submerged and watched in disbelief. Today I spoke to Fanie, and I don’t know whether he knows to articulate how heartbroken he is, because this behind me is his entire world. Gone”.

VO
Floods are generally natural disasters.
But this one was man-made... when 12 sluice gates were opened with little advance warning, taking hundreds of residents by surprise.

INSERT SOCIAL MEDIA UPDATES THAT LEZANNE WILL SEND LATER 30”

WATER GUSHING

VO
The Vaal and Bloemhof dams have earth filled walls that shouldn’t be allowed to overflow. That’s why sluice gates are opened, releasing water and protecting the integrity of the wall. The Vaal has sixty gates along its dam wall, for this reason. But a decision to open the gates was all too sudden and the river came down with biblical vengeance.

VAAL FLOODS CARD 1
P1022026/P1022044
REFLECTIVE SHOT OF CLAIRE LOOKING AT RIVER
“Known as an iconic tourist destination in the Free state, Parys has been one of the towns hardest hit. Residents and lodge owners only had an hour or two to evacuate their properties as these rapids were making their way down the river”

VO
Prof Graeme Addison has been living on the river for 22 years and has never seen it this vicious.

SUPER@ PROF GRAEME ADDISON: PARYS RESIDENT
VAAL FLOODS\CARD 2
CLIP 0033
11:59:12:32
“I think what happened was a coincidence of factors, they had to open the Vaal dam gates…But at the same time and probably unknown to a lot of the officials, there was a flood on the Rietrivier and those two things converged and it became an uncontrollable spate of water, kind of a virtual tsunami on the river”.

VO
Rietspruit is located in the upper parts of the Vaal Basin and heavy rain in Gauteng increased its flow. It was the start of a natural flood. Question is, did the government recognize this?

SUPER@ PROF GRAEME ADDISON: PARYS RESIDENT
VAAL FLOODS\CARD 2
CLIP 0033
11:59:46:06
“We watched the figures on the department of water affair and sanitation website. They are not altogether believable or accurate all the time, they do say they are unverified figures. And we noticed that there was a lot of water coming from the Vaal dam, but there was no record of the water coming from the Rietrivier”.

VO
But given the rising dam levels, action could have been taken sooner.

SUPER@FANIE SMITH
VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
09:58:50:04
“Hulle moes geweet het dit is ‘n reënseisoen en hulle moes voor die tyd al begin water oopmaak. Hulle het die water teruggehou tot hy op so 110% kom dan begin hulle sluise oopmaak. Dan maak hulle twee oop, toe is dit vier, toe is dit ses en van ses toe is dit sommer na twaalf toe”.
TRANSLATION: They should have known it is rainy season and should have opened the water sooner. They keep the water back at 110% and only start to open gates then. They opened two, then it was four, then it was six and then suddenly, it was twelve”

VO
But for the government, it's a catch 22. The department of water and sanitation’s Leonard Manus says its a gamble to let water go in anticipation of natural floods and heavy rain.

SUPER@LEONARDO MANUS:
ACTING DEPUTY DIRECTOR INFRASTRUCTURE
DEPARTMENT OF WATER AND SANITATION
ZOOM
00:05:40:11
“What if the water doesn’t arrive or it falls in an adjacent catchment, and you got that benefit from the rain in the catchment?
Then you sit with a man-made drought, and you are responsible for that as well”.

VO
A full dam is government’s first priority.

SUPER@ PROF GRAEME ADDISON: PARYS RESIDENT
VAAL FLOODS\CARD 2
CLIP 0033
12:07:17:32
“The dilemma faced by water affairs, is that when you’ve got a full dam, you want to keep that water because the winter is coming and there will be no rain On the other hand, there is a prediction of heavy rainfall, you gotto let some water go, how much are you gonna let go…”

VO
But why not open sluices when forecasters warn that exceptionally high rainfall is on its way? Like when a cyclone steadily heads in your direction.

VISUAL PAUSE OF HAVOC.

VO Just this week, Cyclone Freddy hit Madagascar, then made its way towards Mocambique. While it decreased in intensity to a tropical storm, forecasts still indicated heavy rain for South Africa.
Despite this, the Department of Water and Sanitation didn’t budge… again.

SUPER@LEONARDO MANUS:
ACTING DEPUTTY DIRECTOR INFRASTRUCTURE
DEPARTMENT OF WATER AND SANITATION
ZOOM
00:04:00:08
STRETCH HOM SODAT HIERDIE EERSTE WOORDE GEADD WORD
“The big word here is may, it may happen.
There is no assurance that that is going to happen as far as any rainfall is concerned”

VO
Government only opens the gates when the deluge arrives, leaving little time for precautions. And, it seems, urgent information doesn’t reach locals in time.

SUPER@ PROF GRAEME ADDISON: PARYS RESIDENT
VAAL FLOODS\CARD 2
CLIP 0033
12:03:02:48
“It is a communication problem. The department of water affairs needs to assign a communication officer to tell the public what is going on”.

SUPER@FANIE SMITH
VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
09:59:59:31
“Van Vaaldam se kant af, die brug se kant af, weet ons niks as hulle begin oopmaak nie”.
TRANSLATION: We don’t ever know when they are going to open…”

VO
The department admits it can do more to get word to residents.

HIER KAN ONS DALK VIR CLAIRE INSIT WAT NA DIE WATER KYK OM HAAR WEER PRESENCE TE GEE
It adds that those affected shouldn’t have built below the 100 year flood line, which indicates the likely level of water during a 100 year flood. It’s an event which has a 1% probability of occuring in any given year.
But experts believe that the flood line on the Vaal has moved because of global warming and continued urbanisation. But these are natural floods, not those caused by the sudden opening of sluice gates.

UPSOUND

VO
Proper communication is at least what’s needed to avoid another catastrophic flood. Without it, people like Fanie can’t prepare and save what little they have left.

SUPER@FANIE SMITH
VAAL FLOODS CARD 2
CLIP0012
10:01:21:31
“Ja ek gaan nogsteeds hier kom bly. Soos ek sê, genade van Bo af. Ek sal nie verkoop nie.
10:01:39:46
“My lewe is hierso. Ek sal nie verkoop nie”



PROMOS

11”
VO
Hour by hour the water levels kept rising. It was a catastrophe on the Vaal River when sluice gates were opened and residents were caught unprepared for the flood that was coming their way.


PROMO 1
VO: Heavy rains, rising water levels and the Vaal Dam sluice gates…
UPSOUND: ek gaan nogsteeds hier kom bly. Soos ek sê, genade van Bo af. Ek sal nie sommer verkoop hierso nie.
10:01:39:46
“My lewe is hierso. Ek sal nie verkoop nie”
VO: For residents living downstream… opening twelve sluice gates, meant disaster.


PROMO 2
VO: With little warning… several sluice gates in the Vaal Dam were opened, releasing millions of litres of water…
UPSOUND: “It became an uncontrollable spate of water, kind of a virtual tsunami on the river”.
VO: A catastrophe for residents living downstream…

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Hundreds of residents around the Vaal dam have had to evacuate their homes when 12 sluice gates on the dam were opened. Could there have been earlier warning signs?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Rescue operations were ongoing throughout the weekend to evacuate homes on and around the Vaal dam and river as water levels continue to rise amidst high rain fall. Water affairs have opened 12 sluice gates to manage the inflow, but was it too later?
metadata.Summary: Twelve of the 24 sluice gates on the Vaal Dam have been opened. Given the high rainfall and water moving in from Standerton where the bridge, connecting Mpumalanga and Gauteng have been closed all weekend, rising water levels will urge water affairs to open more sluice gates this week. Problem is, it is all happening at once and hundreds of people living lower downstream have been and will be evacuating their houses.
metadata.Further information: Kyle Streicher and his family had two hours to evacuate their home near Barrage in Vanderbijlpark on Saturday. They returned on Sunday to see whether there was anything to salvage, but their entire home and belongings have been destroyed. Their house was built higher than the 100-year flood mark. And this is where the argument comes in: Firstly: Affected families are angry with water affairs, saying they did not receive proper warning to evacuate in time. Secondly: the gates were opened all at once and should have been done weeks prior to the high rainfall. They say the department of water and sanitation does not have skilled people in place to determine when the gates must be opened. Floods could have been avoided. Two years ago, I did a story on the same topic. People on the Vaal and Lower Orange were concerned that given high rainfall at the time, the department did not open the sluice gates in time and a flood could have destroyed everything. Luckily for them, it turned out that it was never necessary to open many gates. But this year, is an entirely different story. What people have been complaining and warning about, now happened. But the department of water and sanitation in Gauteng is actually a very highly skilled group of people. They say, they opened the first sluice gates on 7 February and there was sufficient warning. They add that people who live below the 100-year flood line mark had it coming as they were never supposed to build their houses there.
